topic: Sputnik's beep started the space age (1957)
claim: On Oct. 4, 1957 the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, a 184-pound aluminum sphere whose radio beeps could be heard around the world, opening the Space Age.

beats.caption: BEEP. BEEP.
beats.vo: One tiny beeping ball changed the world.

beats.caption: OCTOBER 4, 1957
beats.vo: On October fourth, nineteen fifty-seven, the Soviet Union launched Sputnik One into orbit.

beats.caption: 184 POUNDS
beats.vo: A shiny aluminum sphere, a hundred and eighty-four pounds, circling Earth every ninety minutes.

beats.caption: THE WORLD LISTENS
beats.vo: Its only job was a radio beep that amateur radio operators everywhere could hear.

beats.caption: FELLOW TRAVELER
beats.vo: The word Sputnik means fellow traveler.

beats.caption: THE SPACE AGE BEGINS
beats.vo: The world was shocked. The Space Age had begun. Beep.

sources.text: NASA History, 65 Years Ago: Sputnik Ushers in the Space Age (184 pounds, orbit about every 90 minutes, beep signal): https://www.nasa.gov/history/65-years-ago-sputnik-ushers-in-the-space-age/
